conventions.api_helper_usage: Paste once into the DevTools Console of a tab that is signed in as the stated actor: customer/cook-as-customer on https://app.<PREVIEW_DOMAIN>, cook and staff on https://ops.<PREVIEW_DOMAIN>. The helper copies the readable XSRF-TOKEN cookie into X-XSRF-TOKEN exactly like the web apps do (apps/customer-web/src/api.ts) and calls https://api.<PREVIEW_DOMAIN>. If no XSRF-TOKEN cookie exists yet, run `await api('GET','/api/v1/me')` first. Mutating commands need a fresh `Idempotency-Key` (crypto.randomUUID(); allowed pattern [A-Za-z0-9-]{8,128}). VALIDATION_FAILED is HTTP 422, MALFORMED_REQUEST 400 (backend ErrorCode).

recipes.place_pickup_cod_x2: const sl=(await api('GET','/api/v1/kitchens/00000000-0000-4000-8000-0000000bd001/slots')).body.items[0];const q=(await api('POST','/api/v1/quotes',{items:[{mealId:'00000000-0000-4000-8000-0000000bb001',quantity:2}],slotId:sl.id,fulfillmentMode:'PICKUP',paymentMethod:'COD'})).body;const o=await api('POST','/api/v1/orders',{quoteId:q.quoteId,clientRequestId:crypto.randomUUID(),acceptedPolicyVersions:{terms:q.termsVersion,cancellation:q.cancellationPolicyVersion}},crypto.randomUUID());// o.status must be 201; o.body.id = order id, o.body.version = expectedVersion for the next command

conventions.seed_money_facts: Prices are integer piastres: koshari 7500, mahshi 18000, molokhia 12025; zone A delivery fee 3000; synthetic policy tax 0 bps, commission 0 bps; kitchen A deposit 5000 bps (50%), no COD cap; slot 13:00 Africa/Cairo, cutoff 11:00, 20 portions per slot, 10 per meal.
conventions.sql_note: Database checks are read-only SELECTs run through the operator's approved psql channel (never with write credentials, except the isolated-stack immutability case). :'order' is a psql variable holding the order UUID. Column names are from backend/app/src/main/resources/db/migration (V11 customer_order/order_item/stock_allocation/order_event, V12 handover_*, V13 cash_report/ledger_*, V14 notification, V17 support_case, V18 refund/settlement, V24-V25-V28 order_payment/payment_event, V29 request_fingerprint).
conventions.data_hygiene: Cases that place orders leave data behind. Cancel pending orders when finished so capacity returns, and use the 2nd/3rd seeded slot for capacity-sensitive cases. Cases marked destructive change shared kitchen/catalogue settings and state their restore step. Always run the deposit journeys on a PR #9 deployment.
conventions.staff_fixture_note: Staff fixtures (deploy/web-preview/seed-owner-e2e.sql, fixtures.json): FX-STAFF-ADMIN (preview-ops-1) holds only staff.grant + audit.read and cannot self-grant. FX-STAFF-ADMIN-B: staff.grant, audit.read, config.read, config.write, security.mfa_policy, security.mfa_reset (no finance or order permissions). FX-STAFF-OPS: cook.review, content.moderate, order.ops, order.exception_cancel, order.handover_override. FX-STAFF-FINANCE: finance.read, finance.verify, finance.refund_approve, finance.settlement, config.read. FX-STAFF-SUPPORT and FX-MULTIROLE: support.case. A second finance.refund_approve holder (FIN-044) or finance.verify for FX-MULTIROLE (FIN-114) needs a temporary grant by FX-STAFF-ADMIN-B, which requires recent MFA.
conventions.mfa_note: origin/develop's Keycloak realm (infra/identity/matbakhy-realm.json) contains no OTP/acr flow, so every step that requires a recent MFA proof (payment recipient approval, payment decision, handover override, staff grants) returns 403 STEP_UP_REQUIRED there. They are runnable only on a PR #9 deployment after the realm step-up flow is applied (docs/security/mfa-policy.md, Migration and rollout).
conventions.ui_language_note: Customer web, ops web and native default language differs (ops web starts in Arabic). Key assertions give the English label; the Arabic mirror is in apps/*/src/i18n.ts. Run each P0 journey once in Arabic (RTL) and once in English (LTR).
conventions.browser_profiles: Use one separate browser profile (cookie store) per actor: all web surfaces share the API session cookie, so a second sign-in in the same profile replaces the first. Run GET /api/v1/me before each actor's steps to confirm identity.
conventions.slot_capacity_rules: Seeded slots (days 1-3) have 20 portions each and 10 per meal; preparation consumes capacity permanently. Default assignment: ORDER-101 and FIN-101 day 1, ORDER-102, FIN-039 and FIN-106 day 2, ORDER-114/115 day 3. Day 1 = Cairo today+1, day 2 = today+2, day 3 = today+3. Before each case read the aggregate availablePortions from GET /api/v1/kitchens/<id>/slots (aggregate only) and the meal-specific availablePortions from the meal's nextSlots (GET /api/v1/meals/<mealId>); switch day if short.
conventions.statement_definitions: Statement 'Cash verified' = SUM(cash_obligation.amount_minor) WHERE state VERIFIED for the kitchen's orders whose COMPLETED event is inside the Cairo date range (default: current Cairo calendar month through today); assert increases, not absolutes. Banner text: 'No platform commission: the whole order amount is yours.' ('(owner decision D10)' appears only on the operating-configuration screen).

cases.title: Cook statement shows completed orders, cash states and no commission; only the owner kitchen's data
prerequisites: Preview stack reachable: customer web https://app.<PREVIEW_DOMAIN>, cook/staff web https://ops.<PREVIEW_DOMAIN>, API https://api.<PREVIEW_DOMAIN>. seed-preview.sql is applied: on the customer web home, kitchen 'مطبخ المعاينة' lists 'Preview koshari' (EGP 75.00) and 'Preview mahshi' (EGP 180.00), and kitchen 'مطبخ تجريبي تاني' lists 'Preview molokhia' (EGP 120.25).
FX-COOK-A signs in at https://ops.<PREVIEW_DOMAIN> and the tab bar shows 'Orders' (ar: الطلبات); GET /api/v1/cook/dashboard in that session returns 200.
In the DevTools Console of the signed-in tab, define the helper `api` from conventions.api_helper (needed for the API steps).
At least one completed order with cash REPORTED/VERIFIED and one with cash DUE at kitchen A today (Africa/Cairo).

Each actor uses a SEPARATE browser profile (or private window/cookie store): customer web, ops web and the API share one session cookie (SecurityConfiguration), so signing in as a second actor in the same profile silently replaces the first. Before each actor's steps run `await api('GET','/api/v1/me')` (helper in conventions.api_helper) and confirm the displayName is that actor.

steps.action: Ops web > 'Statement': leave the default range (month to date), press 'Show'. Read the summary and the table.
Set 'From' after today and press 'Show'.
Console: GET /api/v1/cook/statements?from=2020-01-01&to=2026-12-31 (range over 366 days).
Console: GET /api/v1/cook/statements as the customer.

ui: Summary rows 'Completed orders', 'Order value', 'Cash not reported', 'Cash reported', 'Cash verified'; notice 'The cash you collect is yours. Includes refunds and settlements.'; table columns #, Date, Total, 'Report cash collected' (cash state text) and no commission column. Future range: zero completed orders.
api: Range over 366 days: 422 VALIDATION_FAILED fieldErrors [{to,'RANGE_MAX_366_DAYS'}]. Customer: 403 FORBIDDEN.
database: Statement totals equal SQL over completed orders of kitchen A in the Cairo date range (events with to_state = 'COMPLETED' inside [from 00:00, to+1 00:00) Africa/Cairo).

conventions.api_helper_usage: Paste once into the DevTools Console of a tab that is signed in as the stated actor: customer/cook-as-customer on https://app.<PREVIEW_DOMAIN>, cook and staff on https://ops.<PREVIEW_DOMAIN>. The helper copies the readable XSRF-TOKEN cookie into X-XSRF-TOKEN exactly like the web apps do (apps/customer-web/src/api.ts) and calls https://api.<PREVIEW_DOMAIN>. If no XSRF-TOKEN cookie exists yet, run `await api('GET','/api/v1/me')` first. Mutating commands need a fresh `Idempotency-Key` (crypto.randomUUID(); allowed pattern [A-Za-z0-9-]{8,128}). VALIDATION_FAILED is HTTP 422, MALFORMED_REQUEST 400 (backend ErrorCode).

recipes.place_pickup_cod_x2: const sl=(await api('GET','/api/v1/kitchens/00000000-0000-4000-8000-0000000bd001/slots')).body.items[0];const q=(await api('POST','/api/v1/quotes',{items:[{mealId:'00000000-0000-4000-8000-0000000bb001',quantity:2}],slotId:sl.id,fulfillmentMode:'PICKUP',paymentMethod:'COD'})).body;const o=await api('POST','/api/v1/orders',{quoteId:q.quoteId,clientRequestId:crypto.randomUUID(),acceptedPolicyVersions:{terms:q.termsVersion,cancellation:q.cancellationPolicyVersion}},crypto.randomUUID());// o.status must be 201; o.body.id = order id, o.body.version = expectedVersion for the next command

conventions.seed_money_facts: Prices are integer piastres: koshari 7500, mahshi 18000, molokhia 12025; zone A delivery fee 3000; synthetic policy tax 0 bps, commission 0 bps; kitchen A deposit 5000 bps (50%), no COD cap; slot 13:00 Africa/Cairo, cutoff 11:00, 20 portions per slot, 10 per meal.
conventions.sql_note: Database checks are read-only SELECTs run through the operator's approved psql channel (never with write credentials, except the isolated-stack immutability case). :'order' is a psql variable holding the order UUID. Column names are from backend/app/src/main/resources/db/migration (V11 customer_order/order_item/stock_allocation/order_event, V12 handover_*, V13 cash_report/ledger_*, V14 notification, V17 support_case, V18 refund/settlement, V24-V25-V28 order_payment/payment_event, V29 request_fingerprint).
conventions.data_hygiene: Cases that place orders leave data behind. Cancel pending orders when finished so capacity returns, and use the 2nd/3rd seeded slot for capacity-sensitive cases. Cases marked destructive change shared kitchen/catalogue settings and state their restore step. Always run the deposit journeys on a PR #9 deployment.
conventions.staff_fixture_note: Staff fixtures (deploy/web-preview/seed-owner-e2e.sql, fixtures.json): FX-STAFF-ADMIN (preview-ops-1) holds only staff.grant + audit.read and cannot self-grant. FX-STAFF-ADMIN-B: staff.grant, audit.read, config.read, config.write, security.mfa_policy, security.mfa_reset (no finance or order permissions). FX-STAFF-OPS: cook.review, content.moderate, order.ops, order.exception_cancel, order.handover_override. FX-STAFF-FINANCE: finance.read, finance.verify, finance.refund_approve, finance.settlement, config.read. FX-STAFF-SUPPORT and FX-MULTIROLE: support.case. A second finance.refund_approve holder (FIN-044) or finance.verify for FX-MULTIROLE (FIN-114) needs a temporary grant by FX-STAFF-ADMIN-B, which requires recent MFA.
conventions.mfa_note: origin/develop's Keycloak realm (infra/identity/matbakhy-realm.json) contains no OTP/acr flow, so every step that requires a recent MFA proof (payment recipient approval, payment decision, handover override, staff grants) returns 403 STEP_UP_REQUIRED there. They are runnable only on a PR #9 deployment after the realm step-up flow is applied (docs/security/mfa-policy.md, Migration and rollout).
conventions.ui_language_note: Customer web, ops web and native default language differs (ops web starts in Arabic). Key assertions give the English label; the Arabic mirror is in apps/*/src/i18n.ts. Run each P0 journey once in Arabic (RTL) and once in English (LTR).
conventions.browser_profiles: Use one separate browser profile (cookie store) per actor: all web surfaces share the API session cookie, so a second sign-in in the same profile replaces the first. Run GET /api/v1/me before each actor's steps to confirm identity.
conventions.slot_capacity_rules: Seeded slots (days 1-3) have 20 portions each and 10 per meal; preparation consumes capacity permanently. Default assignment: ORDER-101 and FIN-101 day 1, ORDER-102, FIN-039 and FIN-106 day 2, ORDER-114/115 day 3. Day 1 = Cairo today+1, day 2 = today+2, day 3 = today+3. Before each case read the aggregate availablePortions from GET /api/v1/kitchens/<id>/slots (aggregate only) and the meal-specific availablePortions from the meal's nextSlots (GET /api/v1/meals/<mealId>); switch day if short.
conventions.statement_definitions: Statement 'Cash verified' = SUM(cash_obligation.amount_minor) WHERE state VERIFIED for the kitchen's orders whose COMPLETED event is inside the Cairo date range (default: current Cairo calendar month through today); assert increases, not absolutes. Banner text: 'No platform commission: the whole order amount is yours.' ('(owner decision D10)' appears only on the operating-configuration screen).

cases.title: Finance and payment endpoints are limited to the granted staff; Finance tab visibility follows the grants
prerequisites: Preview stack reachable: customer web https://app.<PREVIEW_DOMAIN>, cook/staff web https://ops.<PREVIEW_DOMAIN>, API https://api.<PREVIEW_DOMAIN>. seed-preview.sql is applied: on the customer web home, kitchen 'مطبخ المعاينة' lists 'Preview koshari' (EGP 75.00) and 'Preview mahshi' (EGP 180.00), and kitchen 'مطبخ تجريبي تاني' lists 'Preview molokhia' (EGP 120.25).

FX-STAFF-FINANCE (PROVISION) holds finance.read, finance.verify, finance.refund_approve and finance.settlement; the ops web shows its 'Finance' tab (the tab appears only for accounts that may read statements, so finance.verify alone is not enough). Payment recipient approval and payment decisions also need a recent Keycloak MFA step-up (PR #9 realm flow); cash verification, refunds and settlements do not.

Staff accounts for this case are PROVISIONED fixtures: grants are written by the operator (DB insert into user_grant) or by FX-STAFF-ADMIN in the ops 'Staff permissions' screen; granting through the API requires staff.grant AND recent MFA (StaffController), which needs the PR #9 Keycloak step-up flow.
A deposit order D1 in any payment state and a completed order O1; ids known.

Each actor uses a SEPARATE browser profile (or private window/cookie store): customer web, ops web and the API share one session cookie (SecurityConfiguration), so signing in as a second actor in the same profile silently replaces the first. Before each actor's steps run `await api('GET','/api/v1/me')` (helper in conventions.api_helper) and confirm the displayName is that actor.

steps.action: Without a session call: GET https://api.<PREVIEW_DOMAIN>/api/v1/ops/payments?state=DISPUTED.

Console (any tab with the helper): GET /api/v1/ops/payments?state=DISPUTED; GET /api/v1/ops/payment-recipients; GET /api/v1/ops/finance/cash-reports; GET /api/v1/ops/finance/statements?kitchenId=00000000-0000-4000-8000-0000000bd001.
Same four calls, then POST /api/v1/ops/orders/<D1>/payment/decision {expectedVersion:0, outcome:'REFUND_OWED', reason:'cook tries staff decision'}.

Sign in to ops web and note the tabs; repeat the four GETs and POST /api/v1/ops/finance/cash-reports/<any uuid>/verification, POST /api/v1/ops/finance/refunds and POST /api/v1/ops/finance/settlements.
Sign in: 'Finance' tab present; the same GETs.

ui: No-grant, support and ops-only staff do not see the 'Finance' tab; finance staff do.
api: Guest: 401 UNAUTHENTICATED. Customer, cook, no-grant/support/ops-only staff: 403 FORBIDDEN on every finance/payment call (the statements probe returns 403 instead of 404). Finance staff: 200 on the GETs. The payment decision additionally returns 403 STEP_UP_REQUIRED without a recent MFA proof.
database: audit_event shows DENIED/absent entries for the forbidden attempts; no order_payment, cash_report, refund or settlement_batch row changed.

unverified: Whether permission denials are written to audit_event (cash.verify self-verification denial is; generic @PreAuthorize denials may not be).

conventions.api_helper_usage: Paste once into the DevTools Console of a tab that is signed in as the stated actor: customer/cook-as-customer on https://app.<PREVIEW_DOMAIN>, cook and staff on https://ops.<PREVIEW_DOMAIN>. The helper copies the readable XSRF-TOKEN cookie into X-XSRF-TOKEN exactly like the web apps do (apps/customer-web/src/api.ts) and calls https://api.<PREVIEW_DOMAIN>. If no XSRF-TOKEN cookie exists yet, run `await api('GET','/api/v1/me')` first. Mutating commands need a fresh `Idempotency-Key` (crypto.randomUUID(); allowed pattern [A-Za-z0-9-]{8,128}). VALIDATION_FAILED is HTTP 422, MALFORMED_REQUEST 400 (backend ErrorCode).

recipes.place_pickup_cod_x2: const sl=(await api('GET','/api/v1/kitchens/00000000-0000-4000-8000-0000000bd001/slots')).body.items[0];const q=(await api('POST','/api/v1/quotes',{items:[{mealId:'00000000-0000-4000-8000-0000000bb001',quantity:2}],slotId:sl.id,fulfillmentMode:'PICKUP',paymentMethod:'COD'})).body;const o=await api('POST','/api/v1/orders',{quoteId:q.quoteId,clientRequestId:crypto.randomUUID(),acceptedPolicyVersions:{terms:q.termsVersion,cancellation:q.cancellationPolicyVersion}},crypto.randomUUID());// o.status must be 201; o.body.id = order id, o.body.version = expectedVersion for the next command

conventions.seed_money_facts: Prices are integer piastres: koshari 7500, mahshi 18000, molokhia 12025; zone A delivery fee 3000; synthetic policy tax 0 bps, commission 0 bps; kitchen A deposit 5000 bps (50%), no COD cap; slot 13:00 Africa/Cairo, cutoff 11:00, 20 portions per slot, 10 per meal.
conventions.sql_note: Database checks are read-only SELECTs run through the operator's approved psql channel (never with write credentials, except the isolated-stack immutability case). :'order' is a psql variable holding the order UUID. Column names are from backend/app/src/main/resources/db/migration (V11 customer_order/order_item/stock_allocation/order_event, V12 handover_*, V13 cash_report/ledger_*, V14 notification, V17 support_case, V18 refund/settlement, V24-V25-V28 order_payment/payment_event, V29 request_fingerprint).
conventions.data_hygiene: Cases that place orders leave data behind. Cancel pending orders when finished so capacity returns, and use the 2nd/3rd seeded slot for capacity-sensitive cases. Cases marked destructive change shared kitchen/catalogue settings and state their restore step. Always run the deposit journeys on a PR #9 deployment.
conventions.staff_fixture_note: Staff fixtures (deploy/web-preview/seed-owner-e2e.sql, fixtures.json): FX-STAFF-ADMIN (preview-ops-1) holds only staff.grant + audit.read and cannot self-grant. FX-STAFF-ADMIN-B: staff.grant, audit.read, config.read, config.write, security.mfa_policy, security.mfa_reset (no finance or order permissions). FX-STAFF-OPS: cook.review, content.moderate, order.ops, order.exception_cancel, order.handover_override. FX-STAFF-FINANCE: finance.read, finance.verify, finance.refund_approve, finance.settlement, config.read. FX-STAFF-SUPPORT and FX-MULTIROLE: support.case. A second finance.refund_approve holder (FIN-044) or finance.verify for FX-MULTIROLE (FIN-114) needs a temporary grant by FX-STAFF-ADMIN-B, which requires recent MFA.
conventions.mfa_note: origin/develop's Keycloak realm (infra/identity/matbakhy-realm.json) contains no OTP/acr flow, so every step that requires a recent MFA proof (payment recipient approval, payment decision, handover override, staff grants) returns 403 STEP_UP_REQUIRED there. They are runnable only on a PR #9 deployment after the realm step-up flow is applied (docs/security/mfa-policy.md, Migration and rollout).
conventions.ui_language_note: Customer web, ops web and native default language differs (ops web starts in Arabic). Key assertions give the English label; the Arabic mirror is in apps/*/src/i18n.ts. Run each P0 journey once in Arabic (RTL) and once in English (LTR).
conventions.browser_profiles: Use one separate browser profile (cookie store) per actor: all web surfaces share the API session cookie, so a second sign-in in the same profile replaces the first. Run GET /api/v1/me before each actor's steps to confirm identity.
conventions.slot_capacity_rules: Seeded slots (days 1-3) have 20 portions each and 10 per meal; preparation consumes capacity permanently. Default assignment: ORDER-101 and FIN-101 day 1, ORDER-102, FIN-039 and FIN-106 day 2, ORDER-114/115 day 3. Day 1 = Cairo today+1, day 2 = today+2, day 3 = today+3. Before each case read the aggregate availablePortions from GET /api/v1/kitchens/<id>/slots (aggregate only) and the meal-specific availablePortions from the meal's nextSlots (GET /api/v1/meals/<mealId>); switch day if short.
conventions.statement_definitions: Statement 'Cash verified' = SUM(cash_obligation.amount_minor) WHERE state VERIFIED for the kitchen's orders whose COMPLETED event is inside the Cairo date range (default: current Cairo calendar month through today); assert increases, not absolutes. Banner text: 'No platform commission: the whole order amount is yours.' ('(owner decision D10)' appears only on the operating-configuration screen).

cases.title: Native apps: deposit checkout and honest payment wording on iOS and Android
prerequisites: Signed iOS and Android builds pointing at the preview API; Preview stack reachable: customer web https://app.<PREVIEW_DOMAIN>, cook/staff web https://ops.<PREVIEW_DOMAIN>, API https://api.<PREVIEW_DOMAIN>. seed-preview.sql is applied: on the customer web home, kitchen 'مطبخ المعاينة' lists 'Preview koshari' (EGP 75.00) and 'Preview mahshi' (EGP 180.00), and kitchen 'مطبخ تجريبي تاني' lists 'Preview molokhia' (EGP 120.25).

Kitchen A payment profile is the seeded one: deposit 50% (deposit_bps 5000), no COD cap, recipient INSTAPAY 'demo-kitchen@instapay.invalid' / 'Demo kitchen (not a real account)' with recipient_status APPROVED (verify: GET /api/v1/cook/payment-profile as FX-COOK-A).

Each actor uses a SEPARATE browser profile (or private window/cookie store): customer web, ops web and the API share one session cookie (SecurityConfiguration), so signing in as a second actor in the same profile silently replaces the first. Before each actor's steps run `await api('GET','/api/v1/me')` (helper in conventions.api_helper) and confirm the displayName is that actor.

steps.action: On each device: add 2 × 'Preview koshari' (13:00 tomorrow), basket, choose 'Deposit sent straight to the kitchen', 'Calculate total'.
Accept terms, 'Place order', open the order, type reference 'TEST-REF-0003', press 'I sent the deposit'. Press it a second time if the button is still visible.
On the web workspace press 'The deposit arrived (EGP 75.00)'.
Pull to refresh the order on the device.

ui: Quote shows 'Deposit now: 75.00', 'Rest on receipt: 75.00', the InstaPay demo recipient and the note that the platform never receives or holds the money. Status texts: 'Waiting for your deposit' -> 'You reported the transfer; waiting for the kitchen to confirm' -> 'The kitchen reported receiving the deposit'. No wording says 'verified by the bank' or 'paid'. Arabic (RTL) variant uses the ar strings.
api: Same API calls as E2E-FIN-039 steps 1-5; the second report is idempotent (200).
database: SELECT from_state, to_state, actor_type, amount_minor, reference, reason_code FROM payment_event WHERE order_id = :'order' ORDER BY occurred_at, id; -> exactly one CUSTOMER_TRANSFER_REPORTED event per order.

cases.blocked_reason: No signed iOS/Android build pointing at the preview is confirmed; native verification is mandatory but store/TestFlight setup is deferred.

cases.title: Deposit orders that end without a reported transfer expire without a case; a disputed deposit can be closed without funds
prerequisites: Preview stack reachable: customer web https://app.<PREVIEW_DOMAIN>, cook/staff web https://ops.<PREVIEW_DOMAIN>, API https://api.<PREVIEW_DOMAIN>. seed-preview.sql is applied: on the customer web home, kitchen 'مطبخ المعاينة' lists 'Preview koshari' (EGP 75.00) and 'Preview mahshi' (EGP 180.00), and kitchen 'مطبخ تجريبي تاني' lists 'Preview molokhia' (EGP 120.25).
FX-COOK-A signs in at https://ops.<PREVIEW_DOMAIN> and the tab bar shows 'Orders' (ar: الطلبات); GET /api/v1/cook/dashboard in that session returns 200.
A read-only database method approved by the operator is available (psql through the operator channel); replace :'order' with the order UUID.
In the DevTools Console of the signed-in tab, define the helper `api` from conventions.api_helper (needed for the API steps).

Kitchen A payment profile is the seeded one: deposit 50% (deposit_bps 5000), no COD cap, recipient INSTAPAY 'demo-kitchen@instapay.invalid' / 'Demo kitchen (not a real account)' with recipient_status APPROVED (verify: GET /api/v1/cook/payment-profile as FX-COOK-A).

FX-STAFF-FINANCE (PROVISION) holds finance.read, finance.verify, finance.refund_approve and finance.settlement; the ops web shows its 'Finance' tab (the tab appears only for accounts that may read statements, so finance.verify alone is not enough). Payment recipient approval and payment decisions also need a recent Keycloak MFA step-up (PR #9 realm flow); cash verification, refunds and settlements do not.
PR #9 realm step-up for step 4. Two deposit orders: E1 (pending, nothing reported) and E2 (ACCEPTED, customer transfer reported, kitchen already pressed 'Not received' so the payment is DISPUTED).

Each actor uses a SEPARATE browser profile (or private window/cookie store): customer web, ops web and the API share one session cookie (SecurityConfiguration), so signing in as a second actor in the same profile silently replaces the first. Before each actor's steps run `await api('GET','/api/v1/me')` (helper in conventions.api_helper) and confirm the displayName is that actor.

steps.action: Reject E1 with Reason 'Kitchen busy'.
Reload E1.
On E2 (payment DISPUTED, order ACCEPTED) press 'Cancel'.
Finance > 'Payments needing attention' > 'Needs reconciliation' > E2: Decision 'Closed without funds', Reason 'Transfer never arrived (test)', 'Record decision'.
Reload E2.

ui: E1: Payment 'Deposit time ran out', order 'Rejected by the kitchen', no 'Deposit review' case. E2: Payment 'Closed without funds'; no refund input appears on the cook card.
api: E1 payment state EXPIRED. E2: REFUND_OWED never entered; decision 200 state CLOSED_NO_FUNDS. Cook refund endpoint on E2 -> 409 STATE_CONFLICT fieldErrors [{payment,'NO_REFUND_DUE'}].

conventions.api_helper_usage: Paste once into the DevTools Console of a tab that is signed in as the stated actor: customer/cook-as-customer on https://app.<PREVIEW_DOMAIN>, cook and staff on https://ops.<PREVIEW_DOMAIN>. The helper copies the readable XSRF-TOKEN cookie into X-XSRF-TOKEN exactly like the web apps do (apps/customer-web/src/api.ts) and calls https://api.<PREVIEW_DOMAIN>. If no XSRF-TOKEN cookie exists yet, run `await api('GET','/api/v1/me')` first. Mutating commands need a fresh `Idempotency-Key` (crypto.randomUUID(); allowed pattern [A-Za-z0-9-]{8,128}). VALIDATION_FAILED is HTTP 422, MALFORMED_REQUEST 400 (backend ErrorCode).

recipes.place_pickup_cod_x2: const sl=(await api('GET','/api/v1/kitchens/00000000-0000-4000-8000-0000000bd001/slots')).body.items[0];const q=(await api('POST','/api/v1/quotes',{items:[{mealId:'00000000-0000-4000-8000-0000000bb001',quantity:2}],slotId:sl.id,fulfillmentMode:'PICKUP',paymentMethod:'COD'})).body;const o=await api('POST','/api/v1/orders',{quoteId:q.quoteId,clientRequestId:crypto.randomUUID(),acceptedPolicyVersions:{terms:q.termsVersion,cancellation:q.cancellationPolicyVersion}},crypto.randomUUID());// o.status must be 201; o.body.id = order id, o.body.version = expectedVersion for the next command

conventions.seed_money_facts: Prices are integer piastres: koshari 7500, mahshi 18000, molokhia 12025; zone A delivery fee 3000; synthetic policy tax 0 bps, commission 0 bps; kitchen A deposit 5000 bps (50%), no COD cap; slot 13:00 Africa/Cairo, cutoff 11:00, 20 portions per slot, 10 per meal.
conventions.sql_note: Database checks are read-only SELECTs run through the operator's approved psql channel (never with write credentials, except the isolated-stack immutability case). :'order' is a psql variable holding the order UUID. Column names are from backend/app/src/main/resources/db/migration (V11 customer_order/order_item/stock_allocation/order_event, V12 handover_*, V13 cash_report/ledger_*, V14 notification, V17 support_case, V18 refund/settlement, V24-V25-V28 order_payment/payment_event, V29 request_fingerprint).
conventions.data_hygiene: Cases that place orders leave data behind. Cancel pending orders when finished so capacity returns, and use the 2nd/3rd seeded slot for capacity-sensitive cases. Cases marked destructive change shared kitchen/catalogue settings and state their restore step. Always run the deposit journeys on a PR #9 deployment.
conventions.staff_fixture_note: Staff fixtures (deploy/web-preview/seed-owner-e2e.sql, fixtures.json): FX-STAFF-ADMIN (preview-ops-1) holds only staff.grant + audit.read and cannot self-grant. FX-STAFF-ADMIN-B: staff.grant, audit.read, config.read, config.write, security.mfa_policy, security.mfa_reset (no finance or order permissions). FX-STAFF-OPS: cook.review, content.moderate, order.ops, order.exception_cancel, order.handover_override. FX-STAFF-FINANCE: finance.read, finance.verify, finance.refund_approve, finance.settlement, config.read. FX-STAFF-SUPPORT and FX-MULTIROLE: support.case. A second finance.refund_approve holder (FIN-044) or finance.verify for FX-MULTIROLE (FIN-114) needs a temporary grant by FX-STAFF-ADMIN-B, which requires recent MFA.
conventions.mfa_note: origin/develop's Keycloak realm (infra/identity/matbakhy-realm.json) contains no OTP/acr flow, so every step that requires a recent MFA proof (payment recipient approval, payment decision, handover override, staff grants) returns 403 STEP_UP_REQUIRED there. They are runnable only on a PR #9 deployment after the realm step-up flow is applied (docs/security/mfa-policy.md, Migration and rollout).
conventions.ui_language_note: Customer web, ops web and native default language differs (ops web starts in Arabic). Key assertions give the English label; the Arabic mirror is in apps/*/src/i18n.ts. Run each P0 journey once in Arabic (RTL) and once in English (LTR).
conventions.browser_profiles: Use one separate browser profile (cookie store) per actor: all web surfaces share the API session cookie, so a second sign-in in the same profile replaces the first. Run GET /api/v1/me before each actor's steps to confirm identity.
conventions.slot_capacity_rules: Seeded slots (days 1-3) have 20 portions each and 10 per meal; preparation consumes capacity permanently. Default assignment: ORDER-101 and FIN-101 day 1, ORDER-102, FIN-039 and FIN-106 day 2, ORDER-114/115 day 3. Day 1 = Cairo today+1, day 2 = today+2, day 3 = today+3. Before each case read the aggregate availablePortions from GET /api/v1/kitchens/<id>/slots (aggregate only) and the meal-specific availablePortions from the meal's nextSlots (GET /api/v1/meals/<mealId>); switch day if short.
conventions.statement_definitions: Statement 'Cash verified' = SUM(cash_obligation.amount_minor) WHERE state VERIFIED for the kitchen's orders whose COMPLETED event is inside the Cairo date range (default: current Cairo calendar month through today); assert increases, not absolutes. Banner text: 'No platform commission: the whole order amount is yours.' ('(owner decision D10)' appears only on the operating-configuration screen).

actors.note: Self sign-up is disabled (registrationAllowed=false, no SMTP, phone OTP never exposed), so these are pre-created Keycloak users with NO app row and an UNVERIFIED phone; the app row is created at first sign-in. Four instances: cases consume them.
Seeded kitchen 'مطبخ المعاينة', pickup + Test zone A delivery, 50% deposit profile, 2 meals.
First staff administrator (STAFF_BOOTSTRAP_SUBJECT): receives staff.grant and audit.read only.
Makes the seeded second kitchen 'مطبخ تجريبي تاني' (1 meal) loginable by re-pointing its existing app_user at the new Keycloak user.
Cook application SUBMITTED, awaiting ops review (consumed by approval cases; it is single-use: a consumed fixture is not reset by re-seeding; use a fresh isolated stack).
Operations: cook approval, moderation, order exceptions.
Second administrator holding the MFA policy/reset permissions (the bootstrap admin cannot self-grant them).
Customer + approved cook (own kitchen) + support staff in one identity.
Disposable Docker Compose stack (never the shared preview). Provisioned by the operator; see fixtures.md.
Signed physical iPhone build (PR #11, owner credentials needed).
Physical Android build (no build pipeline for installable APK distribution yet).

journeys.title: Baseline, public access and identity
journeys.purpose: Record the deployed source SHA, prove public discovery and sign-in/out work and that administration surfaces are not exposed. Run first; later cases cite the SHA it records.

journeys.title: Pickup + cash on receipt: Customer → Kitchen → Operations/Finance/Admin
journeys.purpose: The core order journey: basket and quote, placement, the kitchen accepts/prepares/readies, pickup handover with the customer's code, then operations, finance and the administrator inspect the same synthetic order.

journeys.title: Delivery + cash on receipt
journeys.purpose: Same journey with delivery to Test zone A: fee in the quote, courier hand-off, failure/complete paths, cash due and its verification.

journeys.title: Pickup + 50% direct deposit
journeys.purpose: Manual deposit to the approved (fake) recipient: customer reports transfer, kitchen reports receipt (gate before preparation), remainder in cash, reconciliation.

journeys.title: Delivery + 50% direct deposit, zero platform charges

journeys.title: Guards on the journey: prices, repeats, isolation
journeys.purpose: Server-owned price after a change, immutable placed prices, duplicate submit, a guest basket through sign-in, and isolation between customers and kitchens.

journeys.title: Kitchen workspace and operations control
journeys.purpose: Cook publishes a meal and opens a slot; cross-kitchen access is refused; staff see only what they are granted; a customer cannot make themselves staff; kitchen approval and permission grants (these two need the updated deployment and staff MFA).

journeys.purpose: Optional MFA end to end on the web: enrol, step up, policy authorization, staff high-risk actions. Policies stay OPTIONAL.

# Synthetic demo accounts and test data (no credentials in the repository)

Actors are listed in `fixtures.json`; the cases reference them as `FX-*`. Seven already exist on the preview seed (`deploy/web-preview/seed-preview.sql`). The rest are provisioned by the steps below. **Nothing here has been applied**: provisioning changes a Keycloak realm and a database, so it needs the owner's go on the shared preview, and can be done freely on an isolated stack.

| Already seeded | Extra, to provision |
|---|---|
| FX-CUST-A/B (`preview-customer-1/2`), FX-COOK-A (`preview-cook-1`), FX-STAFF-ADMIN (`preview-ops-1`, only `staff.grant` + `audit.read`), FX-STAFF-NOGRANT (`preview-ops-2`) | FX-COOK-B (makes the seeded second kitchen loginable), FX-COOK-PENDING, FX-STAFF-SUPPORT / -OPS / -FINANCE / -ADMIN-B, FX-MULTIROLE, 4 × FX-CUST-NEW (sign-up is disabled on the preview, so these are pre-created Keycloak users with an unverified phone) |

## Steps (operator)
1. `python3 scripts/owner_e2e_fixtures.py check` — manifest, SQL seed and case files agree.
2. `python3 scripts/owner_e2e_fixtures.py render --out ~/matbakhy-private/owner-e2e-<run>` — writes `credentials.private.json` and `partial-import.json` (random password per user, directory 700, files 600). It refuses a path inside the repository and never prints a password.
3. Create the Keycloak users with a **partial import** (it keeps the fixed user ids that the SQL seed refers to; a plain `create users` call would assign new ids and the grants would not match). On the server, in `deploy/web-preview`:
   ```
   set -a; . ./.env; set +a; export ADMIN_USER="$KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_USER" ADMIN_PASSWORD="$KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD"
   ./kcadm-in-container.sh config credentials --config /tmp/kcadm-e2e.cfg
   ./kcadm-in-container.sh create partialImport -r matbakhy -f - --config /tmp/kcadm-e2e.cfg < ~/matbakhy-private/owner-e2e-<run>/partial-import.json
   ./kcadm-in-container.sh cleanup /tmp/kcadm-e2e.cfg
   ```
   Users that already exist are skipped (their password is not changed).
4. Apply the application rows and grants: `deploy/web-preview/seed-owner-e2e.sql` with the same `psql ... -v issuer=https://id.<PREVIEW_DOMAIN>/realms/matbakhy` call that `./deploy.sh seed` uses. It contains no secrets, does not change a row twice and uses only permission codes that exist on the deployed baseline. After the release with migration V31 is deployed, also apply `deploy/web-preview/seed-owner-e2e-mfa.sql` (grants `security.mfa_policy` and `security.mfa_reset` to FX-STAFF-ADMIN-B); a pre-V31 database rejects those codes.
5. Share the passwords over a private channel (a password manager); delete the private directory after the run. Never paste them into GitHub, tickets, screenshots or logs.
6. Slots: seeded slots exist for three days after seeding. Run `deploy/web-preview/refresh-slots.sql` (additive, repeatable) before a run; do **not** re-run `./deploy.sh seed` (it is not repeatable, and after step 4 its first insert collides).

## Single-use fixtures
On the shared preview the provisioning is one-shot: a consumed fixture (FX-COOK-PENDING once approved, an FX-CUST-NEW once it has signed in) is not reset by re-rendering. Rotating a password needs the Keycloak account console or `kcadm set-password`. Cases that consume fixtures, and all destructive cases, belong on a fresh isolated stack, which is recreated per run. To run on the shared preview again, disable the old users and create new run-specific ones (a new `--out` plus matching rows), or accept that those cases are NOT_RUN.

## Not provided, by design
- TOTP seeds: testers enrol their own authenticator through Keycloak during the MFA cases; nothing stores an OTP secret.
- FX-ISOLATED: a disposable Docker Compose namespace made by the operator; destructive, race and fault cases run only there.
- FX-DEVICE-IOS / -ANDROID: signed physical builds (PR #11 for iOS needs the owner's Apple credentials; there is no Android distribution pipeline yet).
- Seeded meals have no photo, so price-change cases need a meal the cook publishes with a photo.

## Not run
`seed-owner-e2e.sql`, `seed-owner-e2e-mfa.sql`, `refresh-slots.sql` and the render script were checked for consistency with each other and with the migrations' column names; the SQL has **not** been executed against PostgreSQL (NOT_RUN) — run it on the isolated stack first.

# دليل المالك لاختبار مطبخي بنفسك (النسخة التجريبية Preview)

> بيئة تجريبية بحسابات وهمية. مفيش فلوس حقيقية. ماتكتبش أي باسورد في GitHub أو في شات. كل حالة بتفضل **NOT_RUN** لحد ما تتنفّذ فعلًا وتتسجّل نتيجتها (PASS / FAIL / BLOCKED).

## 1) الروابط (دومين `167-86-90-174.sslip.io`)
| الغرض | الرابط |
|---|---|
| موقع العميل | `https://app.167-86-90-174.sslip.io` |
| لوحة المطبخ والعمليات | `https://ops.167-86-90-174.sslip.io` (IP مسموح فقط) |
| الـ API (للقراءة فقط) | `https://api.167-86-90-174.sslip.io/api/v1/configuration/public` |
| تسجيل الدخول (Keycloak) | `https://id.167-86-90-174.sslip.io` — بيفتح تلقائيًا من الأزرار |
| كونسول Keycloak للأدمن | `https://kc-admin.167-86-90-174.sslip.io` (بعد تفعيله؛ بياناته من ملف السيرفر الخاص) |

لو ظهرت "Not available" (403) يبقى الـ IP بتاعك مش في القائمة المسموحة: ابعتلي الـ IP.

## 2) الحسابات (الباسوردات مش هنا)
- موجودة من الأول: `preview-customer-1` / `preview-customer-2` (عملاء)، `preview-cook-1` (مطبخ المعاينة)، `preview-ops-1` (إداري)، `preview-ops-2` (موظف من غير صلاحيات). الباسورد = `PREVIEW_USER_PASSWORD` في `.env` على السيرفر.
- بتتجهّز بعد تشغيل `owner-e2e-provision.sh apply`: `owner-e2e-cook-b`, `owner-e2e-cook-pending`, `owner-e2e-support`, `owner-e2e-ops`, `owner-e2e-finance`, `owner-e2e-admin-b`, `owner-e2e-multirole`, `owner-e2e-cust-new-1..4`. باسوردات كل واحد في ملف `credentials.private.json` في `/srv/matbakhy-backups/owner-e2e-private/<run>/` على السيرفر (صلاحيات 600). **لسه ما اتجهّزتش.**

## 3) قبل ما تبدأ
1. افتح نافذة خاصة (Incognito) لكل حساب.
2. حالة الفحص الأولى (J0) بتتسجّل أولًا: رقم النسخة المنشورة (`./deploy.sh status` على السيرفر).
3. لو الصفحة الرئيسية فاضية (مفيش وجبات) يبقى مواعيد الـ seed انتهت: لازم `refresh-slots.sql` (بيتنفّذ ضمن `apply`).

## 4) أول رحلة كاملة: عميل ← مطبخ ← عمليات/مالية (Pickup + كاش عند الاستلام)
التفاصيل الحرفية لكل خطوة والنتيجة المتوقعة في `generated/core-owner-acceptance-suite.md` (J0 ثم J1). الخلاصة:
1. **J0** (حالات `CFG-001`, `E2E-DISC-001`, `CFG-002`, `E2E-DISC-003`, `CFG-034`): الصفحة الرئيسية بالعربي، الوجبات ظاهرة، تسجيل دخول/خروج، مسارات `/admin` على `id.` بترجع 404.
2. **العميل** `preview-customer-1`: أضف "كشري تجريبي" للسلة (`E2E-BASKET-009`)، غيّر الاستلام/الدفع وشوف إن الإجمالي بيتحسب تاني (`E2E-BASKET-019`)، اطلب **استلام + كاش** (`E2E-ORDER-101`) واحفظ رقم الطلب وكود التسليم.
3. **المطبخ** `preview-cook-1` على `ops.`: اقبل الطلب ← جاري التحضير ← جاهز.
4. **العميل**: اعرض كود الاستلام؛ المطبخ يدخل الكود ويكمّل التسليم.
5. **العمليات/المالية** `owner-e2e-ops` و`owner-e2e-finance` (`E2E-OPS-103`): الطلب مكتمل، الإجماليات بالقروش صح، **مفيش عمولة ولا رسوم منصة**.
6. بعدها: توصيل + كاش (J2)، وديعة 50% (J3/J4)، الحواجز (J5)، المطبخ والصلاحيات (J6)، MFA (J7: السياسات تفضل OPTIONAL)، الأجهزة (J8: محتاج iPhone/Android).

## 5) تسجيل النتيجة
لكل حالة اكتب: رقم الحالة، PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED، لقطة شاشة أو رد الـ API (من غير باسورد/توكن)، وسبب أي فشل. أي FAIL بيتفتح له Issue مربوط برقم الحالة.

## مساحة الاختبار الموحّدة

افتح [تعليمات المعاينة](../../../scripts/testing-workspace/README.md) عشان تستخدم الرحلات والبحث وخطوات الحالات في موقع واحد. الدليل قيد المراجعة: وجود الـ 200 حالة مش معناه إن إرشاداتهم اكتملت أو اتنفّذوا. [مصفوفة التغطية](../testing-workspace/coverage-matrix.md) بتبيّن النواقص لكل حالة.

# Matbakhy owner acceptance testing — execution playbook

**Status: PLAN / NOT_RUN.** This catalog is a test design only. No outcome may be marked PASS without executing and retaining evidence.

## Start here
- Catalog: [owner-acceptance/README.md](owner-acceptance/README.md) → `generated/core-owner-acceptance-suite.md` (run first), `generated/readiness-report.md` (what can be run now), `generated/traceability-matrix.md`.
- Fixtures: [owner-acceptance/fixtures.md](owner-acceptance/fixtures.md).
- Existing sources: [scenario catalog](../../planning/scenarios.json), [roles](../product/06-permissions.md), [state machines](../product/04-state-machines.md), [MFA policy](../security/mfa-policy.md), [preview deployment](../operations/06-web-preview.md).

## Test environments
| Environment | Location | Scope |
|---|---|---|
| Preview web/API/identity | `https://{app,ops,api,id}.<PREVIEW_DOMAIN>` (the current host is in the server `.env`; do not copy it into reports) | Deny-by-default: only the allow-listed customer/staff IPs reach it. Synthetic data only. Non-destructive cases. |
| Keycloak administration | Not published; only through the container (`kcadm-in-container.sh`) or an authenticated SSH tunnel | **Never** expose `/admin` or the master realm. |
| Isolated stack | Disposable Docker Compose namespace | Races, fault injection, REQUIRED/DISABLED policy changes, MFA resets, destructive and reboot drills. |
| Physical iPhone/Android | Signed build | Native step-up, account switch, background/return. CI simulator runs are not equivalent. |

The preview may be older than the repository: read the deployed release with `./deploy.sh status`, and run `./migrate-mfa.sh status` before any MFA case. Cases flagged *needs updated deploy* require the PR #9 release **and** the owner-approved realm migration.

## Order of execution
1. Provision fixtures; run J0 (records the source SHA and image digest used everywhere else).
2. Run J1–J4 (the order journeys) and J5–J6, then the remaining cases by readiness bucket.
3. After the updated deployment and migration: J7 (MFA). Isolated-stack cases on the isolated stack only.
4. Physical devices: J8.

## Single test execution template
Record one result per case in `verification/runs/<run-id>/owner-results.md` or your QA tracking system. Example:

```text
TEST_ID=E2E-ORDER-101
STATUS=NOT_RUN|PASS|FAIL|BLOCKED
SOURCE_SHA=<40-hex SHA>
DEPLOYED_IMAGE_DIGEST=<sha256>
ENV=isolated|preview|physical-iphone
ACTOR=synthetic-customer-a
PRECONDITIONS=<fixture reference, no credentials>
STEPS_RUN=<exact clicks/API requests and inputs>
EXPECTED=<from case>
ACTUAL=<observed>
EVIDENCE=<sanitized screenshot/log path>
DEFECT=<GitHub issue or none>
TESTED_AT=<ISO8601>
```

## Result discipline and regression
- Never claim "all scenarios passed" from successful CI alone. Link actual test IDs to CI jobs or manual evidence.
- Any FAIL opens a tracked defect with reproduction, actual versus expected, source SHA, severity, and an automated regression where feasible.
- Re-run relevant tests after fixes, and run the full core journey suite again before owner approval.
- Tests that require missing signing, unavailable paid integrations, or unperformed live realm migration remain BLOCKED/NOT_RUN.
- Before any live configuration change take a verified backup, record previous policy, and use the documented rollback procedure. Never disable authorization or expose Keycloak admin publicly to simplify tests.

## Completeness review
The authored catalog covers primary positive flows, negative boundary tests, role-based access, payment and pricing integrity, order state machine edges, config combinations and rollback/recovery. It cannot truthfully enumerate every possible input combination; QA should extend cases as new branches, configurations and defects are discovered. Coverage is measured against the canonical product requirements and `planning/scenarios.json`, not by case count alone.

# Public Keycloak admin console (Preview only)

Owner approval 2026-10-19: the Keycloak administration console is reachable from the public Internet at
`https://kc-admin.<preview domain>` (Preview: `https://kc-admin.167-86-90-174.sslip.io`) so the owner can administer the preview realm from a phone on
mobile data or a laptop. **Preview only. It is not approved for staging or production.** Customer sign-in stays on `https://id.<domain>` and is unchanged.

## What is exposed, and what is not

| Path on `kc-admin.*` | Served | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `/` | redirect to `/admin/master/console/` | convenience |
| `/admin`, `/admin/*` | Keycloak | the console and the Admin REST API (every REST call needs a bearer token; none gives 401) |
| `/realms/master`, `/realms/master/*` | Keycloak | the console's sign-in (master realm) |
| `/resources/*`, `/js/*` | Keycloak | console static assets |
| everything else (the `matbakhy` realm, `/health`, `/metrics`, `/welcome`, ...) | **404** | not needed; the customer realm stays on `id.*` |

Not published, ever: Keycloak's management port 9000 (health/metrics), Keycloak 8080, PostgreSQL, SeaweedFS, the API's management port, Grafana. Only
the proxy publishes ports (80/443). `id.*` still answers 404 for `/admin` and `/realms/master`.

## Security controls

1. **Password AND one-time password for every administrator.** The master realm's browser flow is `matbakhy master browser`: cookie, then username+password
   (REQUIRED), then OTP form (REQUIRED, not conditional).
   **There is no public enrolment.** The `CONFIGURE_TOTP` required action is disabled in the master realm, so an account without an OTP simply cannot sign in:
   knowing a password never lets anyone enrol their own authenticator first. Administrators receive their password *and* OTP key from the server
   (`./deploy.sh admin-console create-admin <name>`, below).
2. **No password-only path.** The password grant is switched off for every master client (including `admin-cli`), no master client may override the browser or
   direct-grant flow, and sessions/tokens that predate the hardening are revoked, so the Internet cannot obtain a token or reuse an old cookie with a password alone. Operator tooling (`migrate-mfa.sh`'s kcadm, and `identity/admin_console.py`, which talks to the Admin REST API on the identity container's Docker address) signs in as the service account of the confidential master client
   `matbakhy-ops-cli`; its secret is `KEYCLOAK_OPS_CLIENT_SECRET` in the server's `.env` (mode 600, created by `./deploy.sh render`) and is never printed or committed.
3. **Brute-force protection** in the master realm: 5 failures, then a temporary lock that grows (60 s steps up to 15 min); no self-registration, no reset-password flow.
4. **Dedicated hostname.** `KC_HOSTNAME_ADMIN=https://kc-admin.<domain>` plus the master realm's frontend URL, so the master realm's issuer, sign-in forms,
   cookies and Admin REST all live on `kc-admin.*` (host-only `Secure` cookies; the customer host never sees them). CORS: only the console's own origin is allowed.
5. **Fail closed.** The proxy answers 404 for the whole host unless the file `generated/flags/admin-console-public` exists. `admin-console.sh enable` creates
   it only after hardening, and removes it again if the live verification does not pass. `./deploy.sh admin-console disable` removes it at once.
6. **Not tied to an IP address** (required so a phone on mobile data works); the controls above are the protection.

## Enabling, verifying, closing

The CD workflow runs `./deploy.sh admin-console enable` after every release (idempotent). By hand, on the server:

```
cd /srv/matbakhy-staging/deploy/web-preview
./deploy.sh admin-console status      # hardening, switch, how many users have an OTP
./deploy.sh admin-console enable      # backup, harden, open the switch, verify live (closes again on failure)
./deploy.sh admin-console verify      # live checks only
./deploy.sh admin-console disable     # kc-admin.* answers 404 again
```

`verify` creates a synthetic **read-only** administrator (`verify-admin-<random>`, random password and TOTP secret held in a mode-600 temporary file, rights:
view/query on the matbakhy realm and view-realm on master), signs in through the public URL and checks, with PASS/FAIL/NOT_RUN and exit 0/1/3: the console and
every asset load from the host; the master realm advertises only `kc-admin` URLs; Admin REST refuses no/forged tokens; a **password alone does not sign in** (the OTP
form is required); wrong password and wrong OTP issue no code; the right password plus OTP yields a token whose issuer is `kc-admin.*`; the `admin-cli`
password grant is refused; users, roles, clients and authentication flows of the matbakhy realm are listed through the Admin REST API; a foreign `Origin`
gets no CORS allowance; the read-only account cannot create users or read master users; paths outside the console answer 404; `id.*` is unchanged; internal ports are not
reachable on the public address; an account **without** an OTP cannot sign in and is offered no enrolment. The synthetic administrators are deleted afterwards (a trap; `./admin-console.sh fixture-clean` removes leftovers).

## First sign-in (owner)

The existing bootstrap account (`KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_USER`) has no OTP, so after hardening it **cannot sign in to the console** (that is intended). The first
`enable` therefore creates the owner's administrator `owner-admin` by itself when nobody can sign in yet (name: `ADMIN_CONSOLE_OWNER`); more can be created on the server:

```
./deploy.sh admin-console create-admin <name>      # e.g. a personal account
```

It writes `generated/admin-console/<name>.private` (mode 600, directory 700): the generated password, the one-time-password key (base32) and an `otpauth://` URI.
Read the file on the server (`sudo -u devops cat <GENERATED_DIR>/admin-console/<name>.private`, e.g. `/srv/matbakhy-staging/generated/admin-console/owner-admin.private` where `GENERATED_DIR` is the directory in the server's `.env`), add the account in an authenticator app (iPhone: Passwords or any TOTP app, "enter a setup key" with the base32 key, 6 digits, 30 s), sign in
at the console URL, then **delete the file**. Never paste its contents into chats, tickets or logs. `./deploy.sh admin-console status` lists every master account
as `otp` or `no-otp(cannot-sign-in)`. To replace an administrator (lost phone): `REPLACE=1 ./deploy.sh admin-console create-admin <name>`.

## Rollback

```
./deploy.sh admin-console rollback            # closes the host, rebinds the previous master browser flow, re-enables the admin-cli password grant
PURGE=1 ./deploy.sh admin-console rollback    # also removes the operations client and the master frontend URL
```

The previous flow name and a Keycloak database dump (`keycloak-db-<stamp>.dump`) are written under `$BACKUP_DIR/keycloak/` before any change
(`admin-console-state.env`, parsed as data, never sourced). The `matbakhy` realm, its users, credentials, clients and sessions are never modified by any of this.
To remove the exposure without touching Keycloak: `./deploy.sh admin-console disable`. To remove it from the code: revert the pull request (the host then no longer exists in the Caddyfile).

A lost authenticator is handled with `REPLACE=1 ... create-admin <name>`. Lock-out of everything is a database-level recovery (restore the dump above).
The operations client's secret never appears on a command line (the Admin REST client reads it from the environment).

## What this does not prove

Physical-device sign-in on a phone is the owner's step; the verification above drives the same browser flow over HTTP and is not a rendering test of the console in Safari.

# Keycloak MFA migration of the existing preview realm (D18)

**Status: rehearsed against Keycloak 26.8.0 on a throwaway local instance; NOT yet run on the Contabo preview.** CI success proves the
repository realm files and the application, not that this server's realm was changed. The live run needs a person with Docker access
on the host (`deploy/web-preview`), and its result must be recorded below (see "Evidence of the live run").

Why a migration: the preview deployment imports `identity/matbakhy-realm.preview.json` with `--import-realm`, which **skips a realm that
already exists**. The new MFA flow, authentication levels, `amr` mapper and admin service account therefore have to be applied to the
running realm. Files: `deploy/web-preview/migrate-mfa.sh` (operator entry), `identity/mfa-migration.kcadm.sh` (idempotent kcadm
logic), `kcadm-in-container.sh` (runs kcadm inside the Keycloak container; the admin password and the new client secret never appear
as host command-line arguments), `identity/verify-mfa-flow.py` (checks from outside, through the public proxy).

## What it changes (and what it never touches)
Creates the browser flow `matbakhy browser` (cookie / `matbakhy browser forms` → level 1: username+password, level 2: OTP form, each level
behind a *Level of Authentication* condition; amr references `pwd` / `otp`), sets `acr.loa.map={"mfa":"2"}` on the realm and the web (and
mobile, when present) clients, adds the `oidc-amr-mapper` to those clients, creates the `matbakhy-admin` service-account client with the
realm-management roles `view-users` and `manage-users` only, and **binds the new flow last**. A normal sign-in never asks for OTP; only an
authorization that asks for `acr_values=mfa` does. Users, credentials, sessions, other clients and the built-in `browser` flow are not
modified or deleted. No downtime; the identity container is not restarted.

## Order
1. Deploy the release that contains migration V31 (the CD workflow does it). Until the secret below exists the API starts and everything
   works, but the MFA reset and "end sessions" return 503 / are skipped.
2. The same deploy does this: `deploy.sh up` runs `render` first, which adds `OIDC_ADMIN_CLIENT_SECRET` to `.env` if missing (mode 600 kept) and
   re-renders the (ignored-on-existing-realm) realm file, and compose passes it to the API. Check with `./migrate-mfa.sh status` that `.env` has the secret before step 4.
3. `./migrate-mfa.sh status` — read-only; expect `flows=absent`, `browserFlow=browser`.
4. `./migrate-mfa.sh apply` — runs, in this order: verified database backup (`deploy.sh backup`), a Keycloak database dump and a realm
   export (no users) under `$BACKUP_DIR/keycloak/` (mode 600) plus a state file with the previous browser flow, the migration, and
   `verify`. It takes 3–5 minutes (kcadm starts a JVM per call).
5. `./migrate-mfa.sh status` again — expect `flows=complete`, `browserFlow=matbakhy browser`, `client.matbakhy-admin=present`.
6. `./migrate-mfa.sh verify` can be repeated at any time. It creates a **synthetic user** (`verify-mfa-<random>`, random password and TOTP secret held in a
   mode-600 temp file) through kcadm, signs in with real Keycloak flows, exchanges the codes for tokens and calls the real API through the public proxy:
   a level-1 token must carry the API audience and **no** MFA evidence; a step-up answered with the user's real OTP must carry `acr` in the API's MFA values
   and `amr` `otp`; the API must accept that token when the user turns two-step verification on, **reject** the level-1 token with `STEP_UP_REQUIRED`
   afterwards, and accept the elevated token for the same call; the fixture's preference is switched back off and the user is deleted (only names starting
   `verify-mfa-` are ever removed; `./migrate-mfa.sh fixture-clean` removes leftovers). The final line is `RESULT: PASS`, `RESULT: FAIL` (exit 1) or
   `RESULT: INCOMPLETE` (exit 3, assurance NOT_RUN, never a PASS). `apply` treats exit 3 as "applied, not proven" and prints a warning. The mobile checks stay
   `SKIP` until the beta client is registered (`VERIFY_MOBILE=1` after `docs/mobile/ios-testflight-beta.md` step "register the mobile client"). A first API call by the
   fixture provisions an application account for it; it is a synthetic, inactive-by-use customer record in the preview database (no orders).
7. Manual acceptance with synthetic accounts: a normal customer sign-in on the web app works; Account → Security → turn on two-step verification
   enrols an authenticator through Keycloak; with an administrator account holding `security.mfa_policy`, switching a category to REQUIRED is
   **not** done in this step (policies stay OPTIONAL).

## Idempotence and failure handling
* Re-running `apply` changes nothing when the tree is complete (it only re-sets the admin client secret to the value in `.env`).
* The new flow is bound only after it was built **and verified complete**; if `apply` stops half way the realm still uses the previous flow,
  users are unaffected, and the next run removes the incomplete attempt and builds again. If an incomplete flow is already bound the script refuses
  and asks for `rollback` first.

## Rollback
`./migrate-mfa.sh rollback` rebinds the previous browser flow (read from the state file, which is parsed as validated data and never sourced; the flow name is stored base64-encoded; an unreadable file is refused and you pass `PREVIOUS_FLOW='<name>'` explicitly) and deletes the `matbakhy` flows.
`PURGE=1 ./migrate-mfa.sh rollback` also removes the `matbakhy-admin` client, the `amr` mappers and the `acr.loa.map` attributes.
Users and credentials are untouched either way (an authenticator someone enrolled stays in Keycloak but is unused by the previous flow).
If the identity store itself ever has to be restored: stop `identity`, restore `keycloak-db-<stamp>.dump` from the state file into an empty `keycloak`
database with `pg_restore`, start `identity`. This loses sign-ins and enrolments made after the backup.

## Evidence of the live run (fill in; do not claim before it exists)
| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Date / operator | |
| Release commit running | |
| `status` before / after | |
| `verify` output (PASS lines only, no secrets) | |
| Backup files (names only) | |
| Result | NOT RUN |

## Rehearsal evidence (local, not the live server)
Apply on a realm imported from the pre-D18 preview file, `status` → `flows=complete`, second `apply` → "already complete", normal sign-in of
`preview-customer-1` and `preview-ops-1` still issue a code, a step-up request leads to enrolment, `verify` all PASS, `PURGE=1 rollback`
restores `browserFlow=browser` and removes the admin client and mappers; also run through the `kcadm-in-container.sh` wrapper with a
test double for `docker compose exec`. After the review of `ff64f32`: the assurance verification was run against the same throwaway Keycloak 26.8.0 with a stand-in for the API's MFA contract (the real API needs PostgreSQL and could not be started without Docker), giving `RESULT: PASS`; with no fixture `RESULT: INCOMPLETE` (exit 3); with the `amr` mapper deleted `RESULT: FAIL` on the OTP step-up token. The real API acceptance is exercised only by the live run. The Docker-specific parts (`docker compose exec`, `pg_dump`, `deploy.sh backup`) are exercised only on the server.

# البيئة المحلية

> **Owner role:** Infrastructure and deployment
> **Status:** PARTIALLY IMPLEMENTED — الـ Local Stack المبني على Docker وخوادم Vite للتطوير موجودين (IMPLEMENTED) والـ CI بيجرّبهم على Linux؛ وإجراءات Windows/macOS وتشغيل الـ API برّه Docker هي NOT VERIFIED.
> **Language / اللغة:** [English](local-environment.md) · العربية

سطّب الأدوات الأول ([prerequisites.md](prerequisites-ar.md)). كل حاجة هنا بتستخدم بيانات اصطناعية (Synthetic) وSecrets محلية بس.

## اللي بيوفّره `scripts/dev.sh`

`scripts/dev.sh` (bash) بيلف حوالين `infra/compose.yaml`. الخدمات، من ملف الـ Compose:

| الخدمة | الصورة (مثبّتة بالـ Digest) | بورت الجهاز (الافتراضي، على 127.0.0.1 بس) | الغرض |
|---|---|---|---|
| `postgres` | `postgres:16.15-alpine` | 5432 | قاعدة بيانات التطبيق، وFlyway Migrations بتشتغل مع تشغيل الـ API |
| `identity` | `keycloak/keycloak:26.8.0` في وضع `start-dev` | 8180 | مزود OIDC محلي، والـ Realm بيتعمل له Import من `infra/identity/matbakhy-realm.json` |
| `object-storage` | `adobe/s3mock:5.2.3` | 9090 | محاكي S3 فيه Buckets اسمها `matbakhy-private` و`matbakhy-public` |
| `mail` | `axllent/mailpit:v1.31.5` | 8025 (الواجهة)، 1025 (SMTP) | مصرف بريد؛ مفيش حاجة بتخرج من الجهاز |
| `api` | متبني من `backend/Dockerfile` | 8080 | الـ API بتاع Spring Boot، `APP_ENV=LOCAL`، البروفايل `dev` |

الأوامر (كلها من جذر الـ Repository):

| الأمر | التأثير |
|---|---|
| `scripts/dev.sh doctor` | بيتحقق من المتطلبات المسبقة؛ مابيشغّلش حاجة |
| `scripts/dev.sh up` | `doctor`، وبينشئ ملف الـ env لو ناقص، وبيبني الـ API jar (`./mvnw -DskipTests package`)، وبيرندر الـ Realm، و`docker compose up --build --detach --wait` |
| `scripts/dev.sh smoke` | الصحة، وFlyway baseline، ومناطق التطوير، وOIDC discovery، وS3 buckets، والتقاط البريد، وإنفاذ PKCE، واستجابة 401 للمستخدم المجهول، وتسجيل دخول OIDC من الويب بمستخدم وهمي، ودورة رفع خاص موقّع |
| `scripts/dev.sh down` | بيوقف الـ Containers وبيحتفظ بـ Volume البيانات |
| `scripts/dev.sh reset` | بيوقف ويمسح Volume الـ Stack ده (وبيرفض ملفات env مش معلّمة إنها محلية) |
| `scripts/dev.sh verify` | `doctor` + `up` + `smoke` في مشروع Compose مؤقت على بورتات بديلة (15432، 18180، 18080 ...)، وبيتشال عند الخروج |
| `scripts/dev.sh e2e` | Stack مؤقت، وتطبيقي الويب الاتنين، وبعدها Workflows المتصفح بـ Playwright؛ شوف [test-execution.md](test-execution-ar.md) |

أول تشغيل:

```bash
scripts/dev.sh up
scripts/dev.sh smoke      # prints PASS only if every check passed
```

`up` بينشئ ملف الـ env المحلي (infra/.env، متجاهل من Git) من `infra/.env.example` بكلمات سر عشوائية (صلاحية 600). الملف متجاهل من Git (`.gitignore` بيتجاهل `.env` و`.env.*`) ولازم يحمل `MATBAKHY_ENV_MARKER=local`؛ والسكريبت بيرفض أي ملف تاني. الـ Realm المترندر بيروح على infra/.generated/ (متجاهل من Git). عشان تفصل أكتر من Stack عن بعض اظبط `MATBAKHY_ENV_FILE` و`COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME`.

## المستخدمين الوهميين

الـ Realm المحلي (`infra/identity/matbakhy-realm.json`) بيعرّف `customer-a` و`customer-b` و`cook-a` و`ops-a`، بالإضافة لحساب الخدمة `service-account-matbakhy-admin`. كل المستخدمين ليهم نفس كلمة السر، `DEV_USER_PASSWORD` في ملف الـ env المحلي بتاعك. اقراها من ملفك لما تحتاجها؛ وماتلصقهاش في أي مكان. الـ SMS مش متاح محليًا، وتسجيل الـ MFA التفاعلي المحلي NOT VERIFIED (الـ Realm بيعرّف تدفق OTP في `infra/identity/matbakhy-realm.json`)؛ واختبارات المتصفح بتحاكي التحقق من التليفون بـ SQL (شوف `apps/operations-web/e2e/fixtures.ts`).

بيانات التطوير بتيجي من سكريبتات Flyway المتكررة في `backend/app/src/main/resources/db/devdata` (مناطق خدمة اسمها `test-zone-*`، وسياسة تجارة اصطناعية). `EnvironmentGuard` (`backend/app/src/main/java/com/matbakhy/app/config/EnvironmentGuard.java`) بيرفض البروفايل `dev` أو مواقع devdata لما `APP_ENV` يكون STAGING أو PRODUCTION؛ وLOCAL وCI وPREVIEW بيتحسبوا بيئات اصطناعية.

## الـ Frontends

```bash
corepack enable
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
VITE_API_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8080 pnpm --filter @matbakhy/customer-web dev      # http://localhost:5173
VITE_API_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8080 pnpm --filter @matbakhy/operations-web dev    # http://localhost:5174
```

الخادمين الاتنين بيستخدموا `strictPort`: لو 5173 أو 5174 مشغول بيفشلوا بدل ما ينتقلوا، لأن الـ API بيسمح بالـ Origins دي بالظبط (القيمة الافتراضية لـ `WEB_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` في `backend/app/src/main/resources/application.yaml`) وملف الـ Compose بيظبط التحويل بعد تسجيل الدخول على `http://localhost:5173/`. `VITE_DEMO_NOTICE` بيتحكم في بانر بيئة الـ Demo (شوف `apps/customer-web/src`). تسجيل الدخول بيستخدم تدفق Session Cookie بتاع الـ API (`/oauth2/authorization/keycloak`)، فافتح التطبيقات على `localhost` مش `127.0.0.1` — لأن الـ OIDC issuer هو `http://localhost:8180/realms/matbakhy`.

## الموبايل (تطبيق العميل)

`apps/customer-mobile` تطبيق Expo SDK 57 / React Native 0.86. الإعدادات بتيجي من متغيرات `EXPO_PUBLIC_*` (`EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL` و`EXPO_PUBLIC_OIDC_ISSUER` و`EXPO_PUBLIC_ENVIRONMENT` و`EXPO_PUBLIC_OIDC_CLIENT_ID` و`EXPO_PUBLIC_NOTIFICATION_PROMPT`) بقيم افتراضية في `apps/customer-mobile/app.json` وتحقق في `apps/customer-mobile/src/config.ts`.

```bash
pnpm --filter @matbakhy/customer-mobile start     # Expo dev server
(cd apps/customer-mobile && pnpm bundle:native)    # Android + iOS JS bundles, no native toolchain needed
```

التشغيل على Emulator أو Simulator محتاج الـ Native Toolchains وDevelopment Build؛ ومجلدات `android/` و`ios/` بتتولّد بـ `expo prebuild` ومش بتتعمل لها Commit. Expo Go أو حزمة JS أو معاينة ويب عمرها ما بتتحسب تحقق Native (قاعدة المشروع، شوف [toolchain.md](../../engineering/toolchain.md)). التدفقات الـ Native المتسكربتة موجودة في `apps/customer-mobile/scripts/` وبتشتغل في الـ CI ([ci-cd.md](ci-cd-ar.md)). على الـ Emulator التطبيق بيوصل لـ Stack الجهاز عن طريق الاسم البديل للـ Loopback بتاع الـ Emulator؛ والقيم بالظبط اللي الـ CI بيستخدمها موجودة في `apps/customer-mobile/scripts/auth-roundtrip-android.sh`. جلسة Emulator تفاعلية محلية بإيدك: NOT VERIFIED.

## تشغيل الـ API برّه Docker

`./mvnw spring-boot:run` من `backend/app` محتمل (الـ Spring Boot plugin متظبط في `backend/app/pom.xml`) لكنه NOT VERIFIED هنا. المتطلبات المقروءة من `application.yaml`: `APP_ENV` ملوش قيمة افتراضية ولازم يتظبط (`LOCAL` للتطوير)؛ و`DATABASE_URL` و`DATABASE_USERNAME` و`DATABASE_PASSWORD` افتراضيهم `localhost:5432/matbakhy`؛ و`OIDC_ISSUER` افتراضيه `http://localhost:8180/realms/matbakhy`؛ و`OIDC_WEB_CLIENT_SECRET` والـ Realm لازم يطابقوا اللي `scripts/dev.sh` رندره. أبسط طريقة مدعومة للتكرار على الـ Backend هي `scripts/dev.sh up` وتعيد تشغيله بعد التغييرات (بيعيد بناء الـ jar والصورة).

## الوصول للـ Database وKeycloak (محليًا)

```bash
# psql inside the container (variables come from your env file)
set -a; . infra/.env; set +a
docker compose --env-file infra/.env -f infra/compose.yaml exec postgres psql -U "$POSTGRES_USER" -d "$POSTGRES_DB"
# migrations applied
docker compose --env-file infra/.env -f infra/compose.yaml exec -T postgres psql -U "$POSTGRES_USER" -d "$POSTGRES_DB" -c "SELECT version, success FROM flyway_schema_history ORDER BY installed_rank DESC LIMIT 5"
```

كونسول أدمن Keycloak: `http://localhost:8180`، المستخدم `KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_USER` (الافتراضي `local-admin`)، وكلمة السر `KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD` من ملف الـ env بتاعك. واجهة مصرف البريد: `http://localhost:8025`. تفاصيل أكتر في [run-and-debug.md](run-and-debug-ar.md).

## التنضيف

`scripts/dev.sh down` بيحتفظ بالبيانات؛ و`scripts/dev.sh reset` بيمسح الـ Volume المحلي. الاتنين آمنين للـ Stacks المحلية بس: ماتوجّهش `MATBAKHY_ENV_FILE` لملف مش محلي أبدًا.

## القيود المعروفة وفجوات التوثيق

- [toolchain.md](../../engineering/toolchain.md) بيقول "only Linux has been exercised"؛ وده لسه صحيح لكل إجراء في الصفحة دي.
- مفيش إجراء موثّق لتوصيل تليفون حقيقي بـ Stack شغّال على لاب توب.
